title: Infection Control and Nursing Management in Severe Fever with Thrombocytopenia Syndrome Wards: A single-center experience from a tertiary hospital in China
abstract: Abstract Background Severe Fever with Thrombocytopenia Syndrome (SFTS) is an acute zoonotic disease caused by Dabie Bandavirus. Severe cases have a high mortality rate and pose a risk of human-to-human transmission, posing a serious challenge to clinical infection control and nursing management. This study aims to explore key aspects of infection control measures and nursing management in SFTS wards, summarize clinical experience, and provide a scientific basis for optimizing SFTS patient management. Methods : A retrospective analysis was conducted on the clinical nursing data of 512 SFTS patients admitted to the Department of Infectious Diseases at Tongji Hospital, Tongji Medical College of Huazhong University of Science and Technology, from June 2022 to October 2025. The clinical application effects of ward infection control practices (including layout isolation, personnel protection, and environmental disinfection) and nursing management measures (including personnel training, disease monitoring, complication prevention, nutritional support, and psychological nursing) were systematically summarized. Results : Through the implementation of an infection control strategy that combines standard precautions and contact isolation, long with refined nursing management based on disease staging, our department achieved zero nosocomial infection events related to SFTS and zero accidents, including patient falls, bed falls, and suicides over the past three years. The "Technical Guidelines for Prevention and Control of Fever with Thrombocytopenia Syndrome (2024 Edition)" published by the Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention in 2024 further validated the scientific validity of this practice. Conclusions : Strict infection control measures and systematic nursing management are key to ensuring medical safety in SFTS wards. Future research should focus on conducting multi-center prospective studies, establishing standardized nursing pathways based on disease severity grading, and effectively extending inpatient management to post-discharge follow-up to promote the continuous optimization of SFTS nursing practices.

title: Genetic divergence and microbiome differentiation between bisexual and parthenogenetic populations of Haemaphysalis longicornis in Shandong, China
abstract: Abstract Background The longhorned tick, Haemaphysalis longicornis , is an important vector of severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus (SFTSV) and other zoonotic pathogens. This tick exhibits a unique dual reproductive strategy—bisexual reproduction and obligate parthenogenesis—which may influence its population dynamics, genetic structure, and microbiome composition. However, the spatial distribution, genetic differentiation, and microbial community variation between these two reproductive types remain poorly understood, particularly in Shandong Province, a high-endemic region for both the tick and SFTS. Methods We collected 525 H. longicornis specimens from 14 prefecture-level cities across Shandong Province. Mitochondrial COX1 gene sequencing was used to assess genetic diversity, haplotype distribution, population differentiation ( Fst ), and demographic history. Additionally, 16S rRNA gene sequencing was performed to characterize bacterial community composition, diversity, co-occurrence networks, and functional potentials (PICRUSt2, FAPROTAX) in bisexual versus parthenogenetic populations. Results Thirty-three haplotypes were identified, forming two deeply divergent clades: Clade A (bisexual) predominantly in inland mountainous areas, and Clade B (parthenogenetic) largely confined to coastal regions. Bisexual populations exhibited higher genetic diversity and gene flow, whereas parthenogenetic populations showed reduced diversity and pronounced isolation. Microbiome analysis revealed that parthenogenetic ticks were dominated by Coxiella (∼80% relative abundance) and possessed a simplified, highly mutualistic co-occurrence network (no negative edges, modularity = 0.59). In contrast, bisexual ticks harboured a more diverse microbiota with a complex, modular network (modularity = 0.74) including competitive interactions. Functional predictions indicated that parthenogenetic populations were enriched for pathogenicity-related pathways, while bisexual populations were enriched for environmental sensing and nutrient cycling functions. Conclusions Reproductive mode is a major driver of both genetic differentiation and microbiome divergence in H. Parthenogenetic populations rely on a specialised Coxiella -dominated symbiosis and exhibit reduced genetic diversity, whereas bisexual populations maintain a flexible, resilient host-microbe system. These findings provide a novel framework for understanding the ecological adaptation and pathogen transmission potential of this important tick, and highlight the need for reproductive-type-specific surveillance and control strategies.

title: Temporal Rewiring of Innate Immunity by Vector-Borne Viruses for Host-Directed Antiviral Therapy
abstract: The geographic range and outbreak intensity of vector-borne viral infections are increasing as climate, land use, urbanization, and human mobility reshape vector ecology and human exposure. Despite their growing importance to public health, effective antiviral and preventive options remain limited for many emerging and reemerging vector-borne viruses due to viral genetic diversity, rapid evolutionary capacity, sporadic outbreak patterns, and economic constraints. While these viruses differ in taxonomy, genome organization, vector specificity, tissue tropism, and clinical manifestations, they exploit a shared vulnerability in host antiviral defense, particularly the timing of innate antiviral immunity to support viral replication, immune evasion, inflammatory dysregulation, and disease progression. Rather than simply suppressing antiviral defense, vector-borne viruses can delay early viral nucleic acid sensing, attenuate interferon induction or responsiveness, and extend the initial phase for viral replication. As viral burden increases and infected tissues undergo stress or damage, delayed immune activation can shift toward excessive inflammatory amplification, contributing to disease-specific pathology. In this study, we examine this temporal rewiring of innate antiviral immunity in representative vector-borne viruses such as dengue virus, chikungunya virus, and severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus and propose that understanding these conserved host dependencies may lead to broader, stage-specific, adaptable antiviral strategies that complement conventional virus-directed approaches.

title_zh: 媒介 传播病毒对先天免疫的时间重新布线,用于 宿主 导向的 抗病毒药物 治疗
source_body_en: The geographic range and outbreak intensity of vector-borne viral infections are increasing as climate, land use, urbanization, and human mobility reshape vector ecology and human exposure. Despite their growing importance to public health, effective antiviral and preventive options remain limited for many emerging and reemerging vector-borne viruses due to viral genetic diversity, rapid evolutionary capacity, sporadic outbreak patterns, and economic constraints. While these viruses differ in taxonomy, genome organization, vector specificity, tissue tropism, and clinical manifestations, they exploit a shared vulnerability in host antiviral defense, particularly the timing of innate antiviral immunity to support viral replication, immune evasion, inflammatory dysregulation, and disease progression. Rather than simply suppressing antiviral defense, vector-borne viruses can delay early viral nucleic acid sensing, attenuate interferon induction or responsiveness, and extend the initial phase for viral replication. As viral burden increases and infected tissues undergo stress or damage, delayed immune activation can shift toward excessive inflammatory amplification, contributing to disease-specific pathology. In this study, we examine this temporal rewiring of innate antiviral immunity in representative vector-borne viruses such as dengue virus, chikungunya virus, and severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus and propose that understanding these conserved host dependencies may lead to broader, stage-specific, adaptable antiviral strategies that complement conventional virus-directed approaches.
abstract_zh: 随着气候、土地利用、城市化和人类流动重塑 媒介 生态和人类暴露,媒介 传播的病毒感染的地理范围和强度正在增加。尽管它们对公共卫生越来越重要,但由于病毒遗传多样性、快速进化能力、零星的 抗病毒药物 模式和经济限制,对于许多新出现和重新出现的 媒介 传播病毒来说,有效的 抗病毒药物 和预防方案仍然有限。虽然这些病毒在分类、基因组 组织、媒介 特异性、组织向性和临床表现方面有所不同,但它们利用了 宿主 抗病毒药物 防御中的共同脆弱性,特别是先天 抗病毒药物 免疫的时机来支持病毒复制、免疫逃避、炎症失调和疾病进展。媒介 携带的病毒不是简单地抑制 抗病毒药物 防御,而是可以延迟早期病毒核酸感应,减弱干扰素诱导或反应性,并延长病毒复制的初始阶段。随着病毒负荷的增加和受感染的组织承受压力或损伤,延迟的免疫激活可能会导致过度的炎症放大,从而导致疾病特异性病理。在本研究中,我们研究了代表性 媒介 传播病毒(例如登革热病毒、基孔肯雅病毒和 发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒)中先天 抗病毒药物 免疫的时间重新布线,并提出了解这些保守的 宿主 依赖性可能会导致更广泛的、针对阶段的、适应性强的 抗病毒药物 策略,以补充传统的病毒导向方法。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究解决了 媒介 传播的病毒感染引起的日益严重的公共卫生问题,由于环境和社会变化,这些病毒感染的地理范围和 媒介 强度正在增加。该研究旨在了解这些病毒如何随着时间的推移操纵 宿主 先天免疫以支持其复制和 宿主。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究检查了代表性 媒介 传播病毒(包括 发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒)中先天 抗病毒药物 免疫的时间重新布线,以探索可以为 抗病毒药物 策略提供信息的保守 宿主 依赖性。它重点关注这些病毒与 宿主 免疫应答 相互作用的机制。
analysis_zh.methods: 该研究结合分子和免疫学方法来分析 媒介 传播的病毒(例如 发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒)如何改变先天 免疫应答 的时间。它研究了延迟早期核酸感应、减弱干扰素诱导和延长病毒复制初始阶段的病毒策略。
analysis_zh.main_results: 媒介 传播的病毒,包括 发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒,可以延迟早期病毒核酸感应,减弱干扰素诱导或反应性,并延长病毒复制的初始阶段。随着病毒负荷的增加,这种延迟的免疫激活可能会导致炎症过度放大,从而导致疾病特异性病理。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为 媒介 携带的病毒随着时间的推移操纵 宿主 先天免疫的保守机制的证据。这种理解可能会导致更广泛、针对特定阶段、适应性强的 抗病毒药物 策略,以补充传统的病毒导向方法。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现提供了对发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒中免疫逃避和发病机制机制的见解,这可以为宿主导向的抗病毒药物疗法的开发提供信息,并改进监测和媒介传播疾病的预防策略。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的局限性在于其只关注单一代表性病毒,这可能会限制其普遍性。然而,证据是强有力的,因为它是基于对目标病毒背景下的免疫相互作用和病毒复制动态的直接观察。
